featured_reviews.name: Vivek Venugopalan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Amazing place. Way better than the Matunga south indian restaurants.

Shree Muthappan Eating House is a hidden gem at Bhandup on the Jangal Mangal Road. Appam is the speciality of this place and it is totally worth it. The appam is not the sweet round appam but the Malayalam style Appam like dosa. We also had Sada Dosa which was crispy till the last bite. Sambhar and Chutney are one of the best around Mumbai. Your meal should mandatorily end with filter coffee which has the correct amount of decoction and the required sweetness.

Other specialities are Pazham Pori(Kela Bhajji), Parotta, etc. which we couldn't try.

The hotel is clean and the staff are friendly. Owner is a good person and good to have a conversation with.

You can park your two wheelers outside the restaurant on the road.

The rates are way too economical for the quality of food served.

I would surely visit Muthappan Eating house again.

Cheers.

featured_reviews.name: Sandeepkumar Nishad
featured_reviews.review_text:
During my multiple visits to this hotel, I have observed that they use Delicious Fat Spread instead of real butter in their food. While butter is a dairy product made from milk,Delicious Fat Spread is made from vegetable oils, and the two have very different properties.

Although Delicious Fat Spread is also manufactured by Amul and marketed as a versatile alternative to butter, it is not the same as real Amul Butter. When I asked the hotel staff about it, they claimed they use Amul Butter — but in reality, they use Delicious Fat Spread.

This product may not be as healthy as real butter, especially for those who prefer natural dairy products. My only intention in sharing this review is to make people aware: if you order dishes here that contain butter, you may actually be served fat spread instead.

Please choose your food carefully and stay healthy.
Eat healthy, stay healthy.

Authentic South Indian Flavors & A Perfect Spot for a Quick Bite

Madras Cafe is a legendary spot in Bhandup West that never disappoints. Whether you're a daily commuter or visiting with family, it offers a consistent and high-quality dining experience.

Here are the highlights:

Unbeatable Location: Situated right on LBS Marg, just a 2-minute walk from Bhandup Station, it is incredibly convenient for a quick breakfast before work or a relaxed dinner.

Must-Try South Indian Classics: Their Butter Idli Podi and Mysore Masala Dosa are standout items. The sambhar has that authentic, traditional taste, and the coconut chutney is always fresh.

More Than Just South Indian: One thing that sets this branch apart is the variety. Their Cheese Pav Bhaji and Punjabi Thalis are surprisingly good and highly recommended if you're looking for a heavy meal.

The Filter Coffee: You cannot leave without trying their Authentic Filter Coffee. It’s the perfect way to end a meal or recharge during a busy day.

Service & Vibe: The service is quick and efficient. While it can get crowded during peak hours, the AC section on the first floor offers a more comfortable and relaxed environment for families.

Highly recommended for its hygiene, pocket-friendly prices, and nostalgic vibe!

featured_reviews.name: Nick T
featured_reviews.review_text:
They have started off on the right foot with tasty food and portions that felt worth every rupee.

However, lately it seems they've pulled a fast one by shrinking portion sizes while keeping prices on the higher side.

Take the caramel custard for instance—priced ₹126 including taxes, but served in a teacup-sized portion. It’s like being promised a banquet but getting a snack instead, leaving a bad taste in the mouth.

The adage “you get what you pay for” doesn’t seem to hold here anymore.

Initially, it was a bang for the buck, but now it feels like the owners are cutting corners and trying to have their cake and eat it too—expecting customers to pay premium prices for portions that barely satisfy.

It’s a classic case of “the tail wagging the dog,” as the quality still holds up but the stingy portions betray the value. Customer loyalty feels like it’s hanging by a thread when dishes don’t live up to expectations anymore.

On the bright side, the flavors remain rich and true to Punjabi cuisine, so the food itself is still quite tasty if you can look past the downsizing.

The service is decent and the ambience comfortable, but these positives can’t mask the feeling that the place is trying to pull the wool over patrons’ eyes with overpriced small servings.

For what it’s worth, the place has a loyal following, but for new customers, the diminishing portions may prove to be the last straw.

In a city bursting with dining options, Mini Punjab at Bhandup is sadly falling behind the eight ball by not matching quantity with price. It’s a classic “too little, too late” situation, and unfortunately, not even the tastiest curries can save it from being pigeonholed as overpriced for what you actually get.

If they don’t fix this, they risk losing customers who feel their wallets are getting lighter while plates only shrink.

featured_reviews.review_text:
While wandering around recently, I stumbled upon a new place called Mini Punjab, and I'm so glad I did! It’s a cozy, small restaurant, but don't let the size fool you — it packs a big punch when it comes to cleanliness, hospitality, and most importantly, flavor.

The hygiene here is top-notch — everything was spotless, from the dining area to the kitchen. That alone made a great first impression. But what really stood out was the politeness and helpful nature of the staff. They were welcoming, attentive, and genuinely cared about the customer experience, which is rare these days.

Now, let’s talk about the food — absolutely mouth-watering! Every dish we ordered was full of rich flavors and cooked to perfection. You can tell they use quality ingredients and authentic Punjabi recipes. Whether you're a foodie or just someone looking for a good meal, this place won’t disappoint.

And to top it off, the prices were moderate and totally worth it for the taste and service offered.

Highly recommended if you're in the area and craving some delicious Punjabi cuisine. Will definitely be visiting again soon!

featured_reviews.name: Prasad K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bhau Vada Pav – A Bhandup Classic

Bhau Vada Pav is easily one of the best spots in Bhandup for vada pav—and that’s not just nostalgia talking. I’ve been eating here since childhood. It used to be just around the corner from my school, and I’d treat myself to a vada pav every now and then. Decades later, not much has changed, and that’s a good thing.

Their vada pav has always been slightly more expensive than other stalls, but it’s worth every rupee. The quality stands out. The vada is large, crispy on the outside, soft inside, and full of flavor. It’s sandwiched in a generously sized pav with their signature red garlic chutney, plus a couple of fried green chilies on the side. Best eaten hot—when the flavors really come alive.

Even today, the quality is exactly how I remember it. That kind of consistency is rare.

They do offer other snacks, but honestly, I’ve never felt the need to try anything beyond the vada pav—it’s that good. The shop is usually crowded, with no seating. You either stand inside and eat or get it packed to go.

If you’re in Bhandup and haven’t had Bhau’s vada pav, you’re missing out. It’s a must-try.

This extra charge is not mentioned anywhere, which is misleading for customers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Ruined Evening – Terrible Service & Absolute Lack of Basic Etiquette
​Rating: 1/5 stars
​We had an incredibly frustrating experience at Pop Tate's. While the food was okay, the service was outright appalling and completely ruined our evening.
​We arrived when the restaurant was busy, but even after it emptied out, we ended up sitting there for almost three hours due to pure negligence.
​The Food and the Missing Ingredients:
We ordered the jalapeno cheese balls, but they were served completely missing the jalapeno. When we pointed this out, the server offered to replace it with an avocado alternative... which never even arrived.
​The 1-Hour Delay & Lazy Excuses:
I had to follow up with our server three times about our order. After waiting for over an hour, the server's explanation was that the KOT (Kitchen Order Ticket) hadn't printed in the kitchen. What makes this unacceptable is that the server lacked the basic courtesy to check on the delay or inform us beforehand. I eventually had to ask a completely different server just to find out what was happening, and nobody seemed to have a clue. This is exceptionally poor etiquette from the service team.
​Frustrating "Apology":
At the end of the night, the head server came over with a complimentary pastry to apologize. We politely declined, explaining that the team had already ruined our evening and that they needed to train their staff to pay attention to tables and anticipate guest needs. Instead of listening, the server didn't even apologize verbally and simply brought the pastry again after we had already denied it. This just added to our frustration.
​Final Verdict:
Throughout the night, the servers were completely preoccupied chit-chatting with each other instead of managing their tables. I highlighted this directly to the head server. This branch desperately needs strong, strict supervision and heavy retraining for its staff. I sincerely hope management takes this seriously and improves in the near future, but as of now, I cannot recommend this place.
